**3B.6 Research Note: Andrés Manuel López Obrador (2024)**

Bottom line: I found **some narrow, lawful de-escalation and rights language**, but the stronger 2024 record is **negative**: insecurity remained high, journalists and critics were still being targeted, and security policy was widely viewed as feeding a broader climate of fear rather than reducing it.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive, limited | Biden and AMLO agreed to coordinate immediate measures to reduce irregular border crossings while protecting human rights | Reuters | 2024-04-30 | https://theprint.in/world/us-mexico-to-clamp-down-on-illegal-immigration-leaders-say/2062785/ | This is the clearest evidence of a security problem being handled through coordination and human-rights language rather than fear politics or blanket coercion. | 3B.6, 2B.1, 2B.7 |
| Positive, limited | Mexico reaches agreement with Venezuela to deport migrants | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-03-21 | https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/mexico-reaches-agreement-with-venezuela-to-deport-migrants-3348403 | Mexico handled a cross-border pressure point through a formal bilateral agreement, which is at least a narrow example of rule-based administration rather than punitive spectacle. | 3B.6, 2B.7, 3B.5 |
| Positive, limited | AMLO said politics exists to avoid war, urged Iran-Israel not escalate | Presidente de México | 2024-04-13 | https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/la-politica-se-invento-para-evitar-la-guerra-afirma-presidente-sobre-conflicto-en-medio-oriente/ | Public anti-war messaging cuts against direct fear-mongering, though it is external and rhetorical rather than evidence of domestic security improvement. | 3B.6, 2B.1, 2B.6 |
| Negative | Mexico | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-01-25 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/rampant-extortion-reveals-corrosive-hole-in-mexico-security-strategy-3283251 | Reuters reported extortion remained far above AMLO’s starting point, undermining any claim that insecurity was meaningfully reduced. | 3B.6 |
| Negative | Mexico | Amnesty International / CPJ | 2024-03-06 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/mexico-killings-journalists-strengthen-federal-mechanism/ | Journalists under the federal protection mechanism were still being killed, showing that state protection did not reliably reduce fear for high-risk civilians. | 3B.6, 3B.1, 3B.4 |
| Negative | México | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico | The Reuters Institute described AMLO’s final year as marked by continued verbal attacks on journalists, rights advocates, and the media, which supports a broader political fear climate. | 3B.6, 3B.3 |
| Negative | Mexico | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/mexico/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says AMLO persistently attacked the press and demeaning specific reporters and outlets, reinforcing intimidation rather than public reassurance. | 3B.6, 3B.3, 3B.5 |
| Negative | Mexico | Human Rights Watch | 2024-08-30 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/30/mexico-proposed-constitutional-changes-threaten-rights | HRW warned the proposed changes could expand military power and erode privacy and transparency safeguards, which is negative for fear reduction and civilian confidence. | 3B.6, 3B.5, 3B.4 |
| Negative | Mexico’s military’s role in migrant massacre comes under sharp scrutiny | Reuters | 2024-10-16 | https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/mexico-militarys-role-in-migrant-massacre-comes-under-sharp-scrutiny-2024-10-16/ | Reuters reported soldiers killed six migrants, a direct sign that state force could intensify insecurity instead of calming it. | 3B.6, 3B.1, 2B.9, 3B.2 |
| Negative | Mexico | ONU-DH / UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention | 2024-09-17 | https://hchr.org.mx/relatorias_grupos/visita-a-mexico-informe-del-grupo-de-trabajo-sobre-la-detencion-arbitraria/ | The UN Working Group said arbitrary detention remained widespread and linked to torture, disappearances, and arbitrary executions, which is strong evidence against a low-fear, law-governed security climate. | 3B.6, 3B.1, 3B.4, 3B.5 |

**Assessment**

- Best positive evidence is **limited and procedural**: migration coordination with the U.S. and Venezuela, plus anti-war rhetoric.
- Best negative evidence is **strong and sustained**: extortion remained high, journalists were still being killed, the press was attacked repeatedly, and security institutions were criticized for abuse and intimidation.
- Overall, I would rate this lens **negative** for AMLO in 2024.

**Search gap**

- I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence that AMLO materially reduced domestic fear and insecurity at scale.
- I also did **not** find solid evidence that he avoided replacing insecurity with a broader political fear climate; multiple independent sources point in the opposite direction.
